items.title: AI could put people off tech jobs and hurt the economy, warns Raspberry Pi boss
items.originalSummary: Eben Upton warns against claims that Artificial Intelligence will destroy vast numbers of computing roles over the coming years.
items.learningSummary: Eben Upton, founder of Raspberry Pi, has issued a cautionary warning regarding the growing belief that Artificial Intelligence will eliminate substantial numbers of computing positions in the coming years. During a recent industry discussion, Upton expressed concern that pervasive pessimistic messaging about AI-driven automation could potentially discourage young people from pursuing careers in technology. He argues that such negative narratives may create unintended consequences for future economic development. While acknowledging that AI will undoubtedly transform certain aspects of the technology sector, Upton maintains that demand for skilled professionals will remain robust and could even expand. He emphasises the importance of presenting balanced perspectives to ensure emerging generations maintain enthusiasm for entering computing fields. His remarks contribute to an ongoing global debate about automation's disruptive potential and its implications for workforce development.

vocabulary.meaning: significant in size, amount, or degree; considerable
vocabulary.example: The report documented substantial changes in hiring practices across the industry.

vocabulary.meaning: the use of technology to perform tasks with minimal human intervention
vocabulary.example: Increased automation has transformed manufacturing processes over the past decade.

vocabulary.meaning: causing fundamental interruption or significant change to existing systems
vocabulary.example: The disruptive influence of artificial intelligence is reshaping traditional business models.

vocabulary.meaning: strong, healthy, and able to withstand challenging conditions
vocabulary.example: Despite market volatility, the technology sector demonstrated robust growth.

readingQuestions.question: What specific consequence does Upton suggest may result from negative media coverage of AI's impact on employment?
readingQuestions.answer: Upton suggests that pervasive pessimistic media coverage may discourage young people from pursuing technology careers, which could negatively affect future economic growth.

readingQuestions.question: Based on Upton's argument, what inference can be drawn about the relationship between public perception and career choices in the technology sector?
readingQuestions.answer: One can infer that public perception heavily influences career decisions; if young people receive consistently negative messages about AI and employment, they may avoid technology fields altogether, potentially creating a skills shortage.

readingQuestions.question: How is the word 'robust' used in context within the learning summary, and what does it convey about the demand for technology professionals?
readingQuestions.answer: In context, 'robust' describes the demand for skilled technology professionals, conveying that this demand is strong, healthy, and likely to endure despite AI advancements.

items.writingPrompt: Some individuals argue that artificial intelligence will inevitably replace vast numbers of jobs in the technology sector, while others maintain that such concerns are exaggerated and that new opportunities will emerge to offset any losses. Discuss both perspectives and give your own opinion. You should write at least 250 words.
items.listeningText: Eben Upton, founder of Raspberry Pi, has raised concerns about predictions suggesting artificial intelligence will destroy numerous computing roles. He warns that excessive negative messaging about AI-driven automation could discourage young people from pursuing technology careers. During his address, Upton emphasised that while AI will transform certain industries, demand for skilled professionals will likely remain strong. He argues for balanced reporting to ensure future generations remain interested in computing. His comments contribute to broader discussions about automation and workforce development. The tech entrepreneur advocates for more optimistic yet realistic approaches to technological progress.

items.title: King’s College London to merge with Cranfield University
items.originalSummary: Merged institution will become second largest mainstream university in UK with about 47,000 students King’s College London has agreed to merge with Cranfield University, creating a new UK “super-university” that would rival many of its international competitors in size and research output. The merger would result in King’s taking on another 5,000 mainly postgraduate students and becoming the second largest mainstream university in the UK, with about 47,000 students, overtaking the University of Manchester and behind only University College London. items.title: Why universities are rethinking written exams in the age of AI
items.originalSummary: As generative AI tools become widespread, several universities are piloting oral defenses, in-class essays and project-based portfolios to verify what students have actually learned.
items.learningSummary: Universities around the world are experimenting with new assessment formats as the use of generative AI tools spreads on campus. Instead of relying solely on take-home essays, some institutions are introducing oral defenses, in-class writing tasks and project-based portfolios that are harder to outsource. Supporters argue these methods give a more reliable picture of a student's real ability, while critics warn that they can be time-consuming and stressful for both students and staff. Educators broadly agree that the goal is not to ban technology but to redesign tasks so that AI becomes a study aid rather than a shortcut.

vocabulary.example: Universities are revising their assessment methods to keep pace with new technology.

readingQuestions.question: Why are some universities changing their exam formats?
readingQuestions.answer: Because the spread of generative AI tools makes traditional take-home essays harder to verify.

readingQuestions.question: What is one drawback of the new assessment methods mentioned?
readingQuestions.answer: They can be time-consuming and add stress for both students and staff.

readingQuestions.question: What does the word 'outsource' suggest about how some students use AI?
readingQuestions.answer: They hand over the writing work to AI rather than doing it themselves.

items.writingPrompt: Some people think universities should redesign assessments because of generative AI, while others believe traditional written exams remain the fairest test. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
items.listeningText: Universities are quietly rethinking how they assess their students. With generative AI now widely available, take-home essays no longer prove what a student really understands. As a response, several institutions are piloting oral defenses, timed in-class writing and small group projects. Supporters say these formats offer a more reliable view of student learning, especially when combined with regular feedback. Critics, however, point out that they take more time to mark and can feel stressful for those who are not confident speakers. Most educators agree on one thing: the aim is not to fight technology, but to redesign assessments so that AI supports learning instead of replacing it.
